title: Successive vertex orderings of graphs
summary: A successive vertex ordering of a graph is a linear ordering of its vertices in which every vertex except the first has at least one neighbour appearing earlier. Such orderings arise naturally in incremental growth and connectivity-preserving constructions, where vertices are added sequentially and must attach to the existing structure. We derive an exact formula for the number of successive vertex orderings of any finite connected graph.
